This has to be the wildest Claude use case I’ve ever seen. You can now have Claude reply to every single one of your Instagram DMs for you, and turn every person who messages you into an actual follower. It’s done through @manychat, which is officially approved by Meta. Here’s how to set it up in about 2 minutes: 1. In Manychat, go to Settings → Integrations 2. Paste in your Claude API key 3. Build an automation that fires on any DM or comment 4. Add an action block and pick Claude 5. Write out exactly who you are, what you do and how you want it talking to people Step 5 is the part that actually makes the difference. Here’s the trick: Before anyone gets the thing you promised them, have it check whether they’re following you. If they’re not, it asks them to follow first, then sends the resource. Now every DM you get is a chance at a new follower.  #ManychatPartner

How to build a company brain in Slack with AI (Slack + Google Drive + Claude + n8n) How to build an AI company knowledge base inside Slack, so your team stops asking the same questions in DMs. Built for real and tested on Harborline, a 14-person web and marketing agency we set up for this. The tools, in plain words: - Slack is where the team talks. The bot is called @Brain, powered by Claude. - Google Drive holds the brain as Google Docs: an Index page (the map), one page per client, one per service, plus How We Do Things, Decisions and Who Owns What, all linked to each other. - A Raw folder keeps every original message or file exactly as it was, never edited. Three Google Sheets: the approvers, a gaps list, and a change log (the Brain Log). - n8n connects it all with three AI workflows, using n8n's built-in AI agent with Claude Sonnet. How the Slack AI assistant works: 1. A manager adds a ✅ to a Slack message. n8n checks the approvers sheet and saves the original message into Raw, then the AI agent reads the map, opens only the pages that fact touches, and updates every one of them. Old values stay as history ("from $24,000, was $22,000 until 2026-10-27"). 2. Each change is posted in #brain-updates as old → new, with a link to the source. 3. Someone who isn't an approver adds a ✅? Brain replies "a manager needs to ✅ this to make it official" and changes nothing. 4. Drop a Google Doc in the Inbox folder and it gets filed the same way, then moved into Raw. 5. Ask "@Brain who is building the Northgate site, and can they launch it on a Friday?" and get the answer in the thread, with links to both pages it used. 6. Ask something nobody wrote down, and it says "That's not in the brain yet, so I won't guess", then logs the question to the Gaps sheet. 7. Private channels stay private: the bot has four permissions and can't read private channels or DMs. 8. Every Monday, one report: what changed this week, plus what needs fixing: facts that disagree (both quotes checked word for word on their pages, so only real conflicts show up), sections nobody has reviewed in 90 days, and open questions. Why AI chatbots often give wrong answers about your company: when the answer isn't in front of them, they guess. This one has to bring a quote copied word for word from a page it opened, and n8n checks that the quote is really on that page before the answer goes out. Links come from the map, never from the AI. Only pages on the map count as a source, so old files like a 2025 proposal template are never quoted. One honest limit: Brain reads the map every time. Past a few hundred pages, you'd add a search step. Works for agencies, consultants, clinics, online stores, home-services companies and any small business team that runs on Slack and Google Drive.
